papers.title: BTBD9-driven IMPDH2 ubiquitination governs sleep homeostasis by gating adenosine metabolism in the basal forebrain.
papers.summary: Identified a BTBD9-IMPDH2-adenosine pathway in which CRL3(BTBD9)-mediated ubiquitination of IMPDH2 at K195 relieves GTP-dependent allosteric inhibition, limiting adenosine accumulation and sleep pressure in the mouse basal forebrain. Basal forebrain Btbd9 deletion increased NREM sleep and extracellular adenosine, whereas AAV-delivered interfering peptides targeting the BTBD9-IMPDH2 interaction rescued BTBD9 overexpression-induced abnormal wakefulness.

papers.title: Breathing-evoked potentials in humans during wakefulness and sleep.
papers.summary: Using scalp EEG from 729 Cleveland Family Study participants, the authors identified reproducible breathing-evoked cortical potentials during quiet wakeful breathing, including a pre-inspiratory component ~300 ms before inspiration and post-inspiratory peaks ≤3 s after. These potentials persisted in N2, N3, and REM sleep with simplified morphology resembling K-complexes and co-occurring spindle-range activity, and were qualitatively unchanged in participants free of sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.title: A synchronized dual-scale platform combining flexible micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG reveals frequency-dependent cortex-to-skull spectral gain in awake mice.
papers.summary: The authors built a dual-scale platform in awake mice recording 16-channel flexible micro-ECoG and five skull-screw EEG electrodes on a single clock, enabling sample-aligned comparison across 115 ECoG-EEG pairs. Cortex-to-skull spectral gain was not frequency-flat but increased with frequency following a power law and was non-stationary across blocks, indicating that skull EEG relatively preserves high-frequency cortical activity rather than acting as a simple low-pass copy.

papers.title: Sleep-dependent DNA methylation remodeling in basolateral amygdala fear engrams.
papers.summary: Using activity-dependent tagging with methylome and transcriptome sequencing of basolateral amygdala engram neurons after contextual fear conditioning, the authors show fear learning drives coordinated CpG and CpH DNA methylation remodeling specifically in engrams, with CpH methylation as a distinct epigenetic component; post-learning sleep deprivation partially reversed these changes and impaired recall. Multi-omic integration identified Mid1 as a learning- and sleep-regulated methylation target whose BLA-wide and engram-specific knockdown impaired fear memory consolidation.

papers.title: The role of BDNF, CREB, DAT, GFAP and Arc in manic- and OCD-like behavioral phenotypes in both sexes of rats exposed to REM sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Examined behavioral and hippocampal molecular effects of 14 days of REM sleep deprivation in male and female rats, finding hyperlocomotion, decreased anxiety, and increased OCD-like and stereotyped behaviors alongside decreased BDNF, CREB, DAT, and Arc and increased GFAP expression, with more pronounced effects in females except for anxiety-like behavior and CREB.

papers.title: Charting vulnerability of brainstem functional pathways in aging and prodromal synucleinopathy
papers.summary: Using high-resolution 7-T fMRI, the authors mapped connectivity between 58 brainstem nuclei and cortical regions in young adults, older adults, and individuals with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD). Long-range brainstem-cortical connectivity weakened with aging and further in iRBD, but the two conditions affected distinct systems: aging involved arousal- and cognition-related nuclei and association cortex, whereas iRBD involved sleep- and autonomic-related nuclei extending to sensory-motor cortex.

papers.title: EEG network analysis to identify cortical pathology in Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective analysis of preoperative long-term EEG from 71 Lennox-Gastaut syndrome patients, graph-theoretical network analysis around interictal generalized sharp-and-slow waves yielded a clustering coefficient that differentiated favorable-outcome, unfavorable-outcome, and palliative surgery groups (AUC = 0.915). A novel Network Dominance Score lateralized the lesion with 100% accuracy in the favorable-outcome group, whereas unfavorable-outcome patients showed bilateral or incorrectly localized hubs.

papers.title: An EEG-fMRI Jointly Constrained Digital Twin Brain and Its Application in Alzheime's Disease
papers.summary: The authors developed a two-stage digital twin brain framework jointly constrained by fMRI and EEG data and validated it in healthy young and Alzheimer's disease cohorts, where it captured subject-specific multi-scale brain dynamics. AD models reproduced spectral-temporal signatures of cognitive decline linked to simulated excitation-inhibition imbalance, and simulated rTMS responses associated acute EEG normalization with putative E-I rebalancing.

papers.title: Longitudinal Real-Time Quaking-Induced Conversion Analysis of Misfolded α-Synuclein in Idiopathic Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder Patients with Baseline Cerebrospinal Fluid Negativity.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.summary: In a longitudinal study of 43 idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder patients with negative baseline CSF α-synuclein, 20.9% converted to positive over a mean 2.8 years, with converters showing higher burdens of Parkinson's disease biomarkers (hyposmia, abnormal DAT-SPECT, increased REM electromyographic activity). Longer intervals between lumbar punctures were associated with higher conversion, suggesting serial CSF α-synuclein assessments may identify a very early synucleinopathy stage.

papers.title: Linking Circuit Deficits With Electroencephalography Through Computational Modeling for Psychosis Prediction.
papers.summary: No abstract was provided, so the study's specific methods and findings cannot be summarized.

papers.title: Sequential Associations of Sleep Architecture, Nocturnal Oxygenation, and Respiratory Disturbance With a Composite PSG-Derived Rhythm-Event Index.
papers.summary: In 41 patients undergoing polysomnography, a sequential negative binomial regression model found that only higher sleep efficiency was robustly associated with lower composite PSG-derived rhythm-event rate (IRR = 0.946 per percentage point, 95% CI 0.921-0.972), while AHI and other respiratory indices were not independently associated. The authors note the exploratory and hypothesis-generating nature of these findings.

papers.title: Learning discriminative time-frequency representations for EEG segment-level seizure-state classification with channel selection.
papers.summary: The authors propose a reduced-channel EEG framework combining attention-guided channel selection, TMSST/ConceFT time-frequency analysis, and a CNN-BiLSTM classifier for segment-level ictal/preictal/interictal classification. Using a single EEG channel, it achieved 99.28% holdout accuracy and 98.75% on CHB-MIT and Siena respectively, with leave-one-subject-out accuracy exceeding 91% on both databases.

papers.title: Interictal epileptic discharge > 1% associated with cognitive impairment in adult patients with epilepsy: A cross-sectional study based on dose-response relationship and discharge characteristics.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 114 adults with non-symptomatic epilepsy, a sleep interictal epileptiform discharge index >1% remained associated with lower Montreal Cognitive Assessment, associative learning, and verbal fluency scores after adjustment. Wakefulness thresholds and regional specificity were not definitively established, supporting vigilance-state-aware quantification of IED burden.

papers.title: Computational approaches to deep learning-driven EEG analysis for neurological disease diagnosis: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes deep learning computational approaches for EEG-based diagnosis of neurological diseases, covering architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, hybrid models, GANs, autoencoders, LLMs, and transformers across epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and related disorders. It also discusses preprocessing and denoising strategies and identifies limited data, interpretability, inter-subject variability, and clinical translation as key challenges.

papers.title: Algorithmic loops and the developing brain: a narrative review of dopaminergic mechanisms, sleep disruption, and neuroplasticity.
papers.summary: This narrative review proposes a mechanistic framework in which chronic exposure to algorithmically optimized short-form looping video may drive homeostatic striatal D2/D3 receptor downregulation and attentional dysregulation, amplified by disruption of slow-wave sleep and glymphatic clearance. It cites ABCD cohort associations with grey matter volume, reward-circuit activation, and executive function, and proposes a cross-species multimodal longitudinal research program including primate digital self-administration and human polysomnography.

papers.title: A Comparative Review of Performance and Concurrent Cardiac Rhythm Assessment Across Home Sleep Apnea Testing Devices.
papers.summary: This narrative review compared FDA-cleared Type III home sleep apnea testing devices, reporting validation performance against polysomnography by balanced accuracy and their capabilities for multi-night testing and concurrent cardiac rhythm/AF assessment. Among eight devices compared, AcuPebble Ox200 had the highest balanced accuracy at AHI ≥15 (96.5), followed by WatchPAT SW (94.0) and RX-1 Sleep (92.2), and only RX-1 Sleep was described as aiding concurrent quantification of AF burden.

papers.title: Rest-activity rhythm robustness and prospective mood symptoms in adolescence: Moderating effects of chronotype, sleep timing, and reward sensitivity.
papers.summary: In a prospective study of 199 adolescents at risk for bipolar spectrum disorder, this work tested whether reward sensitivity, morningness-eveningness, and sleep timing moderate associations between actigraphy-derived rest-activity rhythm robustness (Circadian Function Index) and mood symptoms six months later. Lower CFI predicted greater hypo/manic symptoms among those with greater eveningness and later sleep midpoint, and greater depressive symptoms among those with later sleep midpoint.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms of cognitive dysfunction in depression: dual-task event-related potentials and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity.
papers.summary: This study compared 30 patients with depression and 30 matched controls using dual-task event-related potentials (N170, N270) and task-phase-dependent EEG functional connectivity (imaginary coherence). Patients showed prolonged N170 and N270 latencies, altered N170/N270 amplitudes, and task-phase-dependent brain network imbalances, with longer latencies associated with more severe depressive symptoms.

papers.title: A transient decrease in night-to-night variability of REM sleep before myocardial infarction
papers.summary: In a matched cohort from the All of Us Research Program (45 first-MI cases, 450 controls) using Fitbit sleep data, night-to-night variability of REM-sleep fraction showed a transient pattern before MI, decreasing at days 30-16 and returning toward baseline over days 15-1 (max-T p<0.001). The SD decrease was not seen before pneumonia, fracture/appendicitis, or all-cause admissions, and person-specific scoring discriminated cases from controls with AUCs up to 0.66.

papers.title: Sleep Strategies and Performance Outcomes in Ultramarathon Runners: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review examined associations between pre-race and intra-race sleep strategies and physical and cognitive performance in ultramarathon runners, including nine studies with 2262 participants. Greater pre-race sleep duration, including sleep extension, was associated with faster finish times, while greater intra-race sleep duration was consistently associated with longer finish times.

papers.title: EEG-based brain effective and functional connectivity predict PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This study used resting-state dry EEG to quantify effective and functional brain connectivity and train machine learning models to predict PET-defined amyloid positivity in cognitively normal individuals. EEG-based models predicted amyloid status with accuracy comparable to or sometimes exceeding plasma p-tau217 and other previously reported predictors, depending on the model.

papers.title: Using High-Performance Liquid Chromatography to Study Alterations in Biogenic Amines in Drosophila Models of Brain Disorders.
papers.summary: This protocol describes HPLC coupled with electrochemical detection for simultaneous quantification of dopamine, serotonin, and octopamine in Drosophila brain tissue, addressing the technical challenge of low nanomolar-to-femtomolar biogenic amine levels. Applied to an alpha-synuclein Parkinson's disease fly model, it revealed significantly elevated dopamine with unchanged serotonin relative to controls, consistent with early compensatory dopaminergic mechanisms.

papers.title: Harnessing AI for Hypothyroidism Monitoring Using Wearable-Derived Heart Rate Data: Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: Developed and validated an AI system (LightGBM) using wearable-derived sleep heart rate data to classify thyroid status and detect hypothyroidism. In the euthyroid/hypothyroid subset, the system achieved 74.6% accuracy (sensitivity 82%, specificity 73.5%) with one reference pair, improving to 78.1% with three reference pairs, and detected 96.3% of severe overt hypothyroidism cases.

papers.title: Theta-band EEG changes following sequential rTMS and tACS in fibromyalgia: A randomized controlled pilot study
papers.summary: In an exploratory randomized controlled pilot study of 10 adults with fibromyalgia, sequential 10-Hz rTMS over left primary motor cortex followed by 10 daily bilateral 10-Hz tACS increased resting-state theta power in the active group but not controls (Time x Group F(1,8)=8.70, p=.018), with larger increases posteriorly. No significant interaction effects were found for delta, alpha, or beta power.

papers.title: Non-linear association between average daily sleep duration and cardiovascular disease in patients with diabetes or prediabetes.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes and metabolic disorders
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2017–2020 data (n=7,835) examined the dose-response relationship between average daily sleep duration and cardiovascular disease in adults with diabetes or prediabetes. Both short (<7 h) and long (≥9 h) sleep were associated with higher CVD odds, with a non-linear threshold at 8.36 h/day: each hour below was linked to 11% lower risk and each hour above to 27% higher risk.

papers.title: Subtle Alterations of Tidal Breathing Variables in Healthy Late Preterm Neonates at Term-Equivalent Age.
papers.summary: Prospective cross-sectional study compared tidal breathing variables in 60 healthy late-preterm and 60 term neonates at term-equivalent age. Late-preterm neonates had modestly lower tPTEF/tE (27.4% vs. 31.2%) and VPTEF/VE, and each additional week of gestational age was associated with a 1.18-percentage-point increase in tPTEF/tE.

papers.title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms
papers.summary: The Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative describes recruitment strategies to enroll individuals before clinically significant motor symptoms via polysomnogram-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and central hyposmia testing, showing all strategies enriched for CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay positivity. RBD+Hyposmia (94%) and Hyposmia+DEB (85%) were more likely CSF aSynSAA+ than RBD-Hyposmia (40%) and Hyposmia-DEB (55%), and CSF aSynSAA+ individuals showed heterogeneity in mood, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of YZG-331 ameliorated insomnia based on the gut microbiota-drug interaction.
papers.summary: Investigated how gut microbiota contribute to the anti-insomnia efficacy and metabolism of YZG-331, showing it regulates microbial tryptophan metabolism and 5-HT production, increases Lactobacillus and Muribaculaceae abundance with Lactobacillus reuteri as a key species, activates the BH4 cofactor system to promote TPH activity, and raises intestinal butyric acid levels. The study provides the first evidence for the gut microbiota's role in YZG-331's therapeutic mechanism and metabolic processing in insomnia.

papers.title: The Portland SEEQ: A Harmonizable Questionnaire for Environmental Exposome Profiling in Prodromal Synucleinopathy
papers.summary: Describes the development and initial application of the Portland SEEQ, a harmonizable questionnaire for environmental exposome profiling, in 83 participants with isolated REM sleep behavior disorder. Definite/probable exposures were common (e.g., pesticides 38.6%, solvents 43.4%), and greater exposure burden was cross-sectionally associated most consistently with autonomic symptom burden but not with longitudinal clinical worsening.

papers.title: Relationships among heart rate variability, sleep disturbances, and fatigue in patients undergoing interventional therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 66 hepatocellular carcinoma patients undergoing interventional therapy examined associations between heart rate variability (HRV) parameters and fatigue and sleep disturbances. Higher mean heart rate and acceleration capacity were associated with more severe fatigue and poorer sleep quality, with mean heart rate remaining significantly associated with fatigue after adjustment (OR=1.098).

papers.title: Sleep quality, circadian rhythm disruption, functioning, and treatment adherence in major depression: a cross-sectional exploratory study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional exploratory study of 110 outpatients with major depression examining sleep quality (PSQI), biological rhythm disruption (BRIAN), functioning, medication adherence, and depression severity. Poorer sleep quality correlated with lower social functioning and adherence and with greater circadian disruption and depression severity, and in regression biological rhythm disruption was the only independent predictor of sleep quality (beta = 0.445, R-squared = 0.429).

papers.title: Systematic Review of the Literature on Associations Between Symptoms, Stress, Resilience, and Epigenetic Aging in Patients With Cancer.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 10 studies examining epigenetic clocks (nine different methods, most commonly Levine, Horvath, and Hannum) in adults with cancer, finding that nine studies linked more severe symptoms (e.g., fatigue, pain, sleep disturbance, neuropathy, depression, anxiety) to epigenetic age acceleration. Only one study each addressed stress and resilience in relation to epigenetic age acceleration, and the authors call for longitudinal work to validate these associations.

papers.title: Latent Transition Analysis of Symptom Burden Before and After Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Postoperative Lung Cancer Patients.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal study of 273 postoperative lung cancer patients assessed before and 12 weeks after pulmonary rehabilitation, latent profile and latent transition analyses identified stable high- and low-symptom-burden classes, with 61.07% of the high-burden class transitioning to low burden. Younger age, no financial burden, satisfactory sleep, and family living were associated with favorable transition, whereas older age and unmarried/divorced status reduced transition odds.

papers.title: Integration of Aromatherapy and Essential Oils in Asthma Symptom Relief: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes preclinical and clinical evidence that essential oils such as lavender, eucalyptus, and peppermint may relieve asthma symptoms via anti-inflammatory, bronchodilatory, and immunomodulatory mechanisms, including reduced airway hyperresponsiveness, oxidative stress, and Th2-mediated inflammation. It evaluates inhalation, topical, and diffusion application methods and safety issues, while concluding that large-scale trials are needed to validate efficacy and optimize protocols.

papers.title: Associations of Smartphone Use Time and Sleep Duration With Academic Performance Among Korean Adolescents by School Level.
papers.summary: Using 2024 Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey data (48,844 students; 31,902 complete cases), this study found that smartphone use >240 min/day was associated with lower academic performance in both middle school (OR 0.47) and high school (OR 0.65) students. Shorter sleep was associated with higher odds of better performance among high schoolers but not middle schoolers, with a significant school level × sleep interaction.

papers.title: Multisystem Outcomes of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Versus Active Comparators in Type 2 Diabetes: A Multicenter Target Trial Emulation.
papers.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
papers.summary: In a multicenter target trial emulation using harmonized electronic health record data from 70,982 propensity-score-matched adults with type 2 diabetes across five UC medical centers, GLP-1 receptor agonists showed 118 robust associations versus active comparators. Risk reductions were strongest for cardiovascular outcomes (e.g., myocarditis/cardiomyopathy HR 0.38 vs SGLT2i, acute myocardial infarction 0.53) plus renal, hematologic, and tobacco-related outcomes, while increased risks appeared for musculoskeletal conditions, diverticular disease, sleep-wake disorders, and menopausal disorders.

papers.title: [Therapeutic play in pediatric hospitalization: a comprehensive care strategy beyond pain management].
papers.summary: This review examines therapeutic play as a non-pharmacological distraction strategy to reduce pain and anxiety during pediatric hospitalization, highlighting its potential to improve children's cooperation and emotional well-being. It emphasizes the need for institutional policies, professional training, and resource allocation to integrate play into standard care.

papers.title: Patient Experiences of Chronic Low Back Pain: Development of a Conceptual Model Based on a Targeted Literature Review and Qualitative Patient Interviews.
papers.summary: The study developed a patient-centered conceptual model of chronic low back pain (CLBP) by combining a targeted literature review and qualitative interviews with 30 U.S. adults, identifying 16 symptom and 120 impact concepts across physical, emotional, and social domains. The model is intended to support content validity of patient-reported outcome measures and highlight the multidimensional burden of CLBP.

papers.title: Multidimensional predictors of psychological distress in dental education: the mediating role of academic stress a structural equation modelling study with competing model specification.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 303 dental students, structural equation modeling showed that academic stress fully mediated the relationship between sociodemographic/lifestyle factors (economic status, gender, year of study, sleep quality) and psychological distress. A transdiagnostic mental distress model and a GAD-7 anxiety-specific model both fit acceptably, supporting academic stress as a central intervention target.

papers.title: A re-tightening suture technique for hemostasis during aortic root remodeling in chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 45-year-old man with chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection who underwent valve-sparing aortic root remodeling and required a re-tightening suture technique to control bleeding from the proximal continuous suture line. Postoperative imaging showed satisfactory root geometry and no residual aortic regurgitation, suggesting the technique is simple and reproducible for difficult suture-line bleeding.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
